To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) a sufficient level of GABAergic inhibition is critical to ensure that temporally correlated synaptic inputs control postsynaptic firing, 2) the strength of GABAergic inputs increases during the critical period of visual cortical plasticity, and 3) the maturation of GABA release properties and the intrinsic properties of GABAergic interneurons during the critical period contribute to this strengthening.

(1) GABAergic inhibition is necessary to ensure that temporally coherent inputs among converging pathways control spike timing of the postsynaptic neuron; (2) GABAergic interneurons in visual cortex mature during the critical period for ocular dominance plasticity by increasing the amplitude and decreasing the decay time constant of IPSCs to pyramidal cells, and by increasing the instantaneous firing rate.

1) a sufficient level of GABAergic inhibition is critical for the temporal coherence of synaptic inputs to determine postsynaptic spike time, and 2) maturation of inhibitory synapses and interneurons during the critical period of plasticity ensures that the temporaly coherent inputs control the spike timing of pyramidal neurons.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of inhibition in shaping the development of visual cortical networks.
how the brain learns to process information in the face of changing sensory environments, and how the mechanisms of learning change with age.
how the maturation of inhibitory synapses and interneurons in the visual cortex influences the development of cortical circuits and plasticity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the maturation of GABA-mediated inhibition promotes strengthening of temporally coherent inputs among convergent pathways, which is critical for Hebbian learning in the visual cortex.

the maturation of GABA-mediated inhibition during the critical period of visual cortex development is necessary and sufficient to ensure that temporal coherences among synaptic inputs, rather then initial strength or number within a pathway, control postsynaptic action potential timing.

the maturation of GABA inhibition during the critical period of development promotes Hebbian mechanisms of ocular dominance plasticity in the visual cortex by strengthening temporally coherent inputs among convergent pathways.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the maturation of GABA inhibition in visual cortex during the critical period promotes the strengthening of temporally coherent inputs, a process that is critical for the induction of ocular dominance plasticity by the Hebbian mechanism.

the maturation of GABA-mediated inhibition promotes strengthening of temporally coherent inputs among convergent pathways, and this process is essential for the induction of synaptic plasticity in binocular neurons.

the maturation of inhibition during the critical period promotes the strengthening of temporally coherent inputs among convergent pathways, which is critical for Hebbian plastic mechanisms to operate.
The main takeaway from our work is that
inhibition is critical to ensuring that temporally coherent inputs control postsynaptic firing, a prerequisite for spike-timing-dependent plasticities to induce Hebbian learning.
inhibition is critical for Hebbian plastic mechanisms to work properly.
